title: A subspace meeting K_alpha^n for a directed family with intersection k meets k^n
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], $k$ regarded as a subfield of $K$. Let $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}$ be a family of subfields of $K$, indexed by a nonempty set $\mathcal A$, such that (1) $k\subseteq K_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in\mathcal A$; (2) $k=\bigcap_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}K_\alpha$; (3) for $\alpha,\alpha'\in\mathcal A$ there is $\alpha''\in\mathcal A$ with $K_{\alpha''}\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_{\alpha'}$. For a subfield $F\subseteq K$ and $n\ge1$ write $F^{\oplus n}\subseteq K^{\oplus n}$ for the set of vectors all of whose coordinates lie in $F$. Then for every $n\ge1$ and every $K$-linear subspace $V\subseteq K^{\oplus n}$ we have $V\cap k^{\oplus n}\ne0$ if and only if $V\cap K_\alpha^{\oplus n}\ne0$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P3 (lemma-intersection-subfields-subspace, line 11418) and its proof (induction on n); the nonemptiness of the index set, implicit in the source, is stated (for an empty index set and V = 0 the 'if' direction fails); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: The forward implication is immediate: if $0\ne v\in V\cap k^{\oplus n}$, then $v\in V\cap K_\alpha^{\oplus n}$ for each $\alpha$, since $k\subseteq K_\alpha$.

For the converse, induct on $n$. If $n=1$, a $K$-subspace $V\subseteq K$ is either $0$ or $K$: a nonzero $x\in V$ gives $1=x^{-1}x\in V$. Since $\mathcal A$ is nonempty and $V\cap K_\alpha\ne0$ for every $\alpha$, $V=K$, whence $1\in V\cap k$. Now suppose $n\ge2$ and the converse holds in dimension $n-1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07P3 (lemma-intersection-subfields-subspace), proof, induction and case n = 1

proof.text: Identify the tail subspace $W=\{(x_2,\ldots,x_n)\in K^{\oplus(n-1)}:(0,x_2,\ldots,x_n)\in V\}$. It is $K$-linear. If $W\cap k^{\oplus(n-1)}\ne0$, adjoining a leading zero proves $V\cap k^{\oplus n}\ne0$. Otherwise the induction hypothesis, applied to $W$ and contraposed, gives an $\alpha\in\mathcal A$ for which $W\cap K_\alpha^{\oplus(n-1)}=0$.

proof.text: Each coordinate $x_i$ of $v$ therefore belongs to every $K_\beta$ contained in $K_\alpha$. Given any $\gamma\in\mathcal A$, condition (3) supplies $\delta$ with $K_\delta\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\gamma$; hence $x_i\in K_\delta\subseteq K_\gamma$. Condition (2) yields $x_i\in\bigcap_\gamma K_\gamma=k$. The leading coordinate $1$ lies in $k$ too, so $0\ne v\in V\cap k^{\oplus n}$, completing the induction.
